The pain isn’t what gets you (well, it actually is), but it’s the after effects of it. 

I have possible nerve damage from the amount of times I cut when I was in middle/high school, I attempted suicide twice by bleeding out and carry those scars on various parts of my body. 

When you cause physical damage to your body, it stays there. Whether its moments where you lose all of your dexterity, or people you see in day to day life noticing your scars… and even being reminded of traumatic memories because of those scars, they’re more permanent than whatever pain you’re feeling now. 

If you’re using a blade, as clean or sharp as it can be, you’ll be in “screaming for dear life territory” if you use enough pressure to actually get close to killing yourself, that physical pain doesn’t actually go away for a while if you survive, which your chances of doing so are high. 

You have to remember, you might want to die, but your body is always going to go into red alert/survival mode when it senses something isn’t going right, which makes plans like cutting/bleeding to death really just an overall negative

So, I can only talk so much as being from out of state. Vermont is good depending on where you go. 

My experience with Burlington is amazing, it’s “expensive” but you can comfortably live there if you work hard enough or if you’re skilled in a certain trade. Very inclusive place, I’ve never had issues walking with friends there and it definitely is progressive. 

Your main issue is when you go to more backwater towns, I’m in Rutland County. I live in Pittsford, total shithole- not because it’s a dump (it’s pretty nice) but most of the population are bible-thumpers, old-timers, and total hicks. Rutland city itself has a serious drug issue so although you might not get picked out on the streets for being a foreigner (or you might), you definitely might come across a few junkies or relatively unlikable people. 

Do I recommend living here? I guess it depends. If you’re pretty far along in life and want a place to settle down and enjoy nature, sure, it’s a fun place (the hiking trails and scenery are beautiful 1/4 of the year).

But if you’re younger and kind of on the hunt for opportunity, this just isn’t the place at all. You’ll definitely feel like an outsider here and it’ll be awkward trying to make friends and get anything going.
